sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 29.10.2018 at about 11.30 p.m, when the Petitioner was riding a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HD-0084 on the Nagarbhavi Terigebhavan road, at that time,
one car bearing Reg. No. KA-41-MA-7905 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6489/2018 motor cycle from behind.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Fortis hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
He had spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other allowances.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was a self employed and was earning 70,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injury, the Petitioner has became disabled and he cannot continue his work.
The said accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MA-7905 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence,
this Petition.
In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondents appeared before the Court through their Counsels and filed their Written statement to the main Petition.

4. The Respondent No.1 has filed its detailed Objection Statement inter-alia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it admitted that it had issued private car package policy in respect of the vehicle and the same was in force as on the date of the accident.
Further it contended that, there was 2 days delay in lodging the complaint to the police.

Further it contended that the insured entrusted the offending vehicle to a person who do not have license to drive at the time of the accident and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
On these grounds it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

sentences.text: The Respondent No.2 has filed his detailed Objection Statement inter-alia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it admitted his ownership of the offending vehicle.

Further he contended that, his car was insured with 1st Respondent vide policy No. 3001/HI- 10651924/00/B00 and valid from 15.12.2017 to 14.12.2018 and the driver of the car had possessed the valid and effective DL.
Hence, he is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, he has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

6. On the rival Pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 29.10.2018 at SCCH 15 6 MVC No.6489/2018 about 11.30 p.m., near Terige Bhavan, Nagarabhavi, Terige Bhavana Road,
Bengaluru., in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Car bearing No.KA-41-MA-7905?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-13.
He also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.14 & 15 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.1 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order for the following :

10. On the other hand, both Respondents had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MA-7905 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-13 and he has re-iterated the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6489/2018 Petition averments in his Chief-affidavit.

sentences.text: P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.

To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Manager, by name Naveen.S as RW.1 and also examined one witness by name Sendhil Kumar as RW.2 and got marked in total 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 i.e.,
Authorisation letter.
Investigation Report, Compact Disk, Certificate u/s.65 B of Evidence Act and Audio-video Authentication report.
In the cross-examination RW.1 has admitted that in Ex.R2 the involvement of the offending Car on the date of accident was mentioned.

Further the police records i.e., Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch clearly shows that the Petitioner was proceedings on the left side of the road and then the driver of the offending car came from behind and dashed to the Petitioner's motorcycle.
It is pertinent to note here that the Charge sheet is SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6489/2018 material document which has not been challenged by the driver of the offending car.

Hence, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MA-7905 by its driver and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 49 years.

Further, in the Aadhaar card i.e.,
Ex.P-12, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 15.07.1967.
The accident took place on 29.10.2018.

That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 51 years, 3 months,
15 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6489/2018 date of accident was 52 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
17. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he is self employed and was earning 70,000/- per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.12,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads:
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-4 issued by the Medical Officer of the Fortis Health Management Limited, SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6489/2018 Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) Abrasion 3 cmx1cm present over left side of neck.
2) Abrasion 5 cmx3cm present over front of left knee.
3) Abrasion 1 cmx1cm present over left foot finger.

As per the opinion of the Doctor, Injury No.1 to 4 are simple and Injury No.5 is grievous in nature.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :

20. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6489/2018 compensation of 25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
21. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Fortis Health Management Limited, Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.8 - Discharge summary of Fortis Health Management Limited shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 30.10.2018 to 31.10.2018.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 2 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of  12,500/- under this head (@ 12,500/- per month ).
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6489/2018 IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES,
EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
22.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 3,000/- (@ 100/- per day)
towards attendants charges, 3,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and 3,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 9,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :

23. The Petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.1,00,000/-
towards medical and other allowances.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced Medical bill at Ex.P9 total amounting to Rs.35,046/-.

I have gone through the Sheshachala.M. Joshi vs Icici Lomb Genn Insn Co Ltd on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37717911/
6 medical bills and the same is accepted.

sentences.text: Hence, by rounding of SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6489/2018 the same, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for  35,050/- under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

24. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident,
he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

25. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. S.A.Somashekhara as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at Fortis hospital.
Further, he assessed the left upper limb disability of the Petitioner at 26% and the whole body disability at 13%.
PW.2 got marked Outpatient record and X-ray at Ex.P14 & 15.
In the cross-examination, PW.2 deposed that he has not treated the Petitioner.

He admitted that, in the back side of the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6489/2018 X-ray Report, the word mal-united was striked out and the word "displaced"
was mentioned.
He denied other suggestions.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
26. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of 12,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to  1,32,000/- (12,500/- x 12 = 1,50,000/-,
1,50,000/-x 11 x 8/100 =1,32,000/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,32,000/- under this head.

SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6489/2018 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
27.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  50,000 /-
2. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  12,500/-
up period Sheshachala.

sentences.text: Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of  2,63,550/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MA-7905.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

In this case, the Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle has contended that a false Complaint was lodged after two days of the accident by the Petitioner by colluding with the insured of the offending vehicle and the police.

In order to substantiate its contention, the Respondent No.1 has examined its Manager Legal by name Naveen as RW.1 and got marked four documents at Ex.R1 to 4 i.e., Authorization letter, Investigation Report, Compact Disk with 65B Certificate and Audio-video Authentication Report.
The Respondent No.1 has also examined the C.O.O of Pro Access Solution by name Sendhil Kumar as RW.2 and he identified his signature on Ex.R4 as Ex.R4a.
In the cross-examination RW.1 deposed that he does not know the police had issued notice to the owner SCCH 15 20 MVC No.6489/2018 and obtained related documents.
Further he deposed that they have issued Notice to the owner of the offending vehicle to produce the document and he has not produced the Copy of the said Notice before the Court.

RW.1 also admitted that in Ex.R4 no report was mentioned about the voice of the Respondent No.2 and he has not produced document to show that the person who issued Ex.R4 had a authority to issue the report.

Further he also admitted that "      
     
        ."

So,
this evidence is clearly shows that there is no specific confirmation about the identification of the driver of the offending vehicle.
RW.2 has deposed that he has issued Ex.R4 stating that there is no editing and tampering in the Ex.R3 CD.
In the cross-examination he deposed that he has not produced his ID card to show about his work and he has not produced document to show that their company is a State Government Recognized Company.

Further he admitted as under:

sentences.text: So, the evidence is only in respect of authentication by RW.2 in respect of Ex.R3.
It is pertinent to note here that the Petitioner got marked Police Notice issued to the owner of the vehicle at Ex.P5 and the Reply given by the owner to the said Notice as Ex.

P6 . Upon going through the Ex.P5, it clearly shows that the I.O has issued Notice to the Respondent No.2 who is the owner of the said offending vehicle and Ex.P6 is the Reply, wherein the Respondent No.2 has mentioned that he was the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
The Respondent No.1 has not examined Investigating Officer who has conducted the investigation in the case and issued the Notice to the owner.
The Charge sheet has been filed by the I.O against the driver of the offending vehicle who was the Respondent No.2 in this petition.
The Respondent No.1 has SCCH 15 22 MVC No.6489/2018 also not examined their Investigating Officer who has issued Ex.R3.
This Charge sheet has not been challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Under such circumstances this tribunal is of the opinion that the Respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the Respondent No.2 was not the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6489/2018  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 2,63,550/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Fortis hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
He had spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other allowances.
